units.title: Foundations for Functions
units.intro: A **relation** is a set of ordered pairs. Domain = all first components; range = all second. A **function** is a relation where each x has exactly one y. Vertical-line test on a graph: a vertical line hits the curve at most once.

cards.title: 1.1.1 Relations
body: In mathematics, there are different symbols that represent relationships between ordered pairs of objects.
In mathematics, these ordered pairs are described in a set form and given a special name.
A relation is a set of ordered pairs and is named using capital letters such as R, S, T, etc.
The set of all first elements of the ordered pairs is called the domain of the relation.

cards.title: 1.1.2 Functions
body: A function is a relation in which every element of the domain is related to exactly one element of the range.
In an arrow diagram, if there are two arrows coming from the same element of the domain, then the relation is not a function.

cards.title: 1.1.3 Graphs of Functions
body: If there exists a vertical line that crosses the graph of a relation at more than one point, then the relation is not a function.
Graphically, the domain of a relation consists of the x-values which lie on the graph of the relation.
The range of the relation consists of the y-values which lie on the graph of the relation.

cards.title: 1.1.4 Function Notation
body: Determine whether R is a function or not.
Since for every value of the independent variable x, there is only one value of the dependent variable y, he concluded that the relation is a function.
Functions are usually named using small letters such as f, g, h, etc.

cards.title: Formula
body: f: x ↦ y · y = f(x)
Inverse exists as a function only if f is one-to-one (horizontal-line test). Swap x and y, then solve for y. Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f in y = x.

cards.title: Inverses Relationships of Functions
body: One-to-one: different x give different y. Linear f(x)=ax+b with a≠0 is one-to-one. f(x)=x² on all reals is not (unless you cut the domain to x≥0).

cards.title: Tip
body: To find an inverse: replace f(x) with y, swap, solve, rename. Then check f(f⁻¹(x))=x on the new domain.

cards.title: More notes
body: Function notation is a machine: drop x in, get f(x) out. f(2) is a number, not a multiplication. Domain exclusions: zeros of a denominator, negatives inside a school-square-root. Piecewise functions change rule by interval — read the conditions.

cards.title: 1.2.2 Inverse of a Function
body: The inverse of a relation R, denoted by R-1, is a relation obtained from R by interchanging the first and second entries of each ordered pair in R.
In measuring temperature, the Celsius scale (y) is a linear function of Fahrenheit scale (x).
On the Celsius scale, the freezing point of water is 0 °C (degrees Celsius) and the boiling point is 100 °C.
